captions.detailed: This 3D model represents one half of a symmetrical, interlocking filament spool hub. It features a wide, flat circular sidewall base with seven large, radially distributed teardrop-shaped cutouts to save material and weight. Rising from the center of this base is a tall, hollow cylindrical hub designed to hold wound filament. The top rim of the cylinder is equipped with an integrated interlocking mechanism consisting of alternating rectangular tabs (clips) and matching slot cutouts, allowing two identical printed halves to snap together securely.
captions.instruction: Design a customizable, 3D-printable filament spool hub in OpenSCAD. The part should consist of a flat circular flange with optional teardrop-shaped cutouts for weight reduction, a central hollow winding cylinder, and an interlocking clip-and-slot connector system on the cylinder rim so that two identical printed halves can snap together to form a complete spool.
captions.factory: The design uses a main module `spoolConnectorFemale` constructed via boolean operations. The base flange is created using a flat `cylinder` unioned with a tall, slightly tapered winding cylinder (`cylinder` with `r1` and `r2`). To form the interlocking tabs, a `for-loop` rotates and translates small `cube` primitives along the top rim. The core of the cylinder is hollowed out using a `difference` operation with a smaller inner cylinder. The teardrop cutouts are generated by a custom `teardrop` module that uses a `for-loop` and `hull` operations on pairs of large and small cylinders, which are then subtracted from the base flange.
